body:
_Migrated from issue #1297, filed 2026-08-02._

Found while restoring `main` after #1295 (see #1296).

## What happened

#1295 merged with red CI, `main` went red, and `.github/workflows/auto-revert.yml` fired as designed. It cut `auto-revert/76ff555`, reverted the entire #1288 fix — 15 files, 466 deletions, including its own regression tests — pushed the branch, then failed:

```
pull request create failed: GraphQL: GitHub Actions is not permitted
to create or approve pull requests (createPullRequest)
```

Run: https://github.com/new-usemame/Calibre-Web-NextGen/actions/runs/30736769962

The orphaned branch has been deleted. `main` is being fixed properly in #1296 (six stale test fixtures + two missing translations, no production code at fault).

## Two problems

**1. It has never worked.** The repo blocks Actions from creating PRs, so every time this workflow fires it pushes a revert branch and then errors out. It reports itself as a failed run on `main` — which is indistinguishable from a real breakage — and leaves a stray branch behind. As a safety net it is decorative.

**2. If the permission were granted, it would be worse than nothing.** As written it:

- fires on a **single** red `Test Suite` run, with no flake tolerance
- reverts the **whole commit**, not the failing part
- labels the revert **`safe-tier-1`**, which auto-merges as soon as CI is green

A flaky test on `main` would open a revert of verified work, the flake would not recur on the revert branch, CI would go green, and it would merge itself. The fix would be gone with no human in the loop. Today's case is exactly the shape: `main` was genuinely red, but the right repair was six lines of test fixture, not deleting the feature and its tests.

## Worth deciding

- Require N consecutive red runs, or a red run reproduced on a re-run, before acting.
- Never let an automated revert carry a self-merging label — a revert of verified work should require a human, which is the one case where waiting is correct.
- Either grant the permission or delete the workflow. A safety net that silently fails every time it fires is worse than none, because it looks like coverage.

Related: the merge that caused this went in with `Fast Tests`, `E2E Tests (SPA)` and `Test Suite Summary` all FAILURE, which merge-gate condition (a) forbids.
title: auto-revert is a dead safety net, and would be dangerous if revived
